purpose: Bimekizumab-Bkzx is used to treat moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adults whose skin condition has not improved enough with other treatments. It helps clear up the thick, scaly, red patches on the skin that psoriasis causes. It may also be used for other inflammatory conditions as approved by your doctor.
how_it_works: Your immune system makes certain proteins called IL-17A and IL-17F that, when overactive, cause the inflammation and rapid skin cell buildup seen in psoriasis. Bimekizumab-Bkzx is a biologic medicine — a special type of drug made from living cells — that specifically blocks both of these proteins. By blocking them, it calms down the overactive immune response and helps your skin heal and clear up.
common_side_effects: Upper respiratory infections like the common cold, oral thrush (a yeast infection in the mouth), headache, injection site reactions such as redness or pain where the shot was given, tinea infections (fungal skin infections), and diarrhea.
warnings: This medication can lower your ability to fight certain infections, so tell your doctor right away if you have signs of infection like fever, chills, or unusual cough. Do not start this medication if you have an active infection, including tuberculosis (TB) — your doctor will test you for TB before you begin. Avoid live vaccines while on this medication. Tell your doctor if you have inflammatory bowel disease, as this drug may make it worse. This is given as an injection under the skin, and a healthcare provider will show you how to use it safely at home.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 320 mg given as two separate injections of 160 mg each, under the skin, at weeks 0, 4, 8, 12, and 16. After that, you will receive 320 mg every 8 weeks as a maintenance dose. Your doctor may adjust this schedule based on how well your skin responds.
